title: C2C-Explorer: An Exploration Framework for Chip-to-Chip Interconnect Architectures in LLM Cloud Computing Systems
evidence_span: C2C-Explorer combines LLM-workload-driven traffic generation, a switch/full-mesh interconnect simulator scaling to 512 chips, metric-guided adaptive Bayesian design-space exploration, and FPGA prototype validation; the official description reports 2.46–8.23% timing error, up to 7.8x simulation acceleration, and a 32-XPU DeepSeek-R1-671B case with 44.1% goodput improvement and 98.4% memory reduction.
problem: LLM multi-chip systems require realistic traffic, scalable C2C simulation, and tractable exploration of an exponentially large interconnect design space.
method_or_artifact: Workload-driven C2C traffic generator, hybrid cycle/event simulator, metric-guided adaptive Bayesian DSE, and open-source exploration framework.
workload_or_benchmark: DeepSeek-R1-671B inference on 32 XPUs plus diverse LLM traffic patterns; prototype and simulator configurations are not fully specified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Switch/full-mesh chip-to-chip interconnects up to 512 chips, validated against FPGA-based prototypes; link technology, chip frequency, and memory hierarchy are unspecified.
limits: The description omits traffic traces, FPGA prototype details, chip/link power, and baseline configuration identities.
Goodput and memory changes are workload/configuration-specific and not a universal interconnect comparison.
Official description only; open-source availability and reproducibility require inspection.

title: Marlin: I/O-Efficient Prefix KV Cache Retrieval for Long-Prefix LLM Serving
evidence_span: Marlin selects a compact query-agnostic subset of prefix tokens, classifies attention heads by sensitivity to choose retrieval policies, and overlaps head-specific KV transfers with attention computation; the official description reports lower TTFT than state-of-the-art methods while maintaining comparable model accuracy without numeric values.
problem: Long-prefix KV caches exceed GPU memory, and host/storage offload creates I/O stalls that increase time to first token.
method_or_artifact: Dispersion-based token selection, sensitivity-guided head classification, and overlap-optimized KV-transfer/attention pipeline.
workload_or_benchmark: Long-prefix LLM inference; models, prefix lengths, storage tier, accuracy metrics, and baseline systems are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: GPU memory with host-memory or storage KV offload and overlapped data transfers; interconnect, storage device, and memory capacity are unspecified.
metrics: Reduced TTFT relative to state of the art
limits: No TTFT values, prefix lengths, model suite, accuracy delta, I/O bandwidth, or storage conditions are supplied.
Token subset quality and head-classification overhead are unresolved.
Official description only; performance and quality claims require paper-level verification.

title: eLLM: Elastic Memory Management Framework for Efficient LLM Serving
evidence_span: eLLM unifies virtual tensor and KV-cache addressing in a flexible GPU memory pool, dynamically inflates/deflates allocations, uses CPU memory as an extension buffer, and applies SLO-aware scheduling; the description identifies a 20% throughput degradation from isolated management and reports up to 2.32x higher throughput over state-of-the-art systems.
problem: Separate activation and KV-cache memory managers prevent sharing and can waste GPU memory during dynamic LLM serving.
method_or_artifact: Virtual tensor abstraction, elastic GPU/CPU memory pooling, runtime allocation inflation/deflation, and SLO-aware lightweight scheduling.
workload_or_benchmark: LLM serving with dynamic weights, activations, and KV caches under SLO constraints; model suite, request traces, and memory sizes are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: GPU memory plus CPU extension buffer and virtualized tensor/KV address spaces; GPU model, PCIe/NVLink path, and allocation granularity are unspecified.
baselines: isolated activation and PagedAttention-style KV management
metrics: 20% throughput degradation attributed to isolated memory management
limits: The description omits model/request distributions, SLO targets, memory capacity, transfer costs, and baseline tuning.
The 20% degradation and 2.32x gain require matched traces and capacity conditions.
Official description only; serving claims require paper-level verification.

title: PIMGRAG: A Heterogeneous PIM Architecture for Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
evidence_span: PIMGRAG places bandwidth-intensive graph-based RAG retrieval near memory and uses software scheduling to orchestrate PIM and GPU execution, reducing off-chip movement and idle time; the official description reports throughput, latency, and energy-efficiency improvements over CPU–GPU and existing PIM baselines without numeric values.
problem: Graph-based RAG retrieval moves large vector and graph data between memory and processors, creating low arithmetic intensity and bandwidth pressure.
method_or_artifact: Heterogeneous PIM retrieval architecture with hardware/software co-design and lightweight PIM/GPU stage scheduling.
workload_or_benchmark: Graph-based retrieval-augmented generation; graph size, embedding model, retrieval algorithm, and query workload are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: PIM memory plus GPU execution pipeline with coordinated stages; memory technology, bandwidth, capacity, and GPU platform are unspecified.
metrics: Throughput, latency, and energy-efficiency improvements reported qualitatively
limits: No numeric gains, graph/query conditions, memory technology, or energy boundary are supplied.
PIM/GPU scheduling overhead and retrieval-quality effects are unspecified.
Official description only; comparative claims require paper-level verification.

title: Pegasus: Personalized and Communication-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts System for Distributed Edge LLM Inference
evidence_span: Pegasus deploys experts using a semantic-relevance heuristic, locally fine-tunes gating parameters, and uses adaptive batching for intra-node scheduling; on distributed edge LLM inference the official description reports 11.8x lower latency than state-of-the-art distributed MoE frameworks.
problem: Edge nodes cannot host all MoE experts, causing query-dependent expert mismatches under memory, compute, and communication constraints.
method_or_artifact: Similarity-based expert placement, personalized local gating, and adaptive-batching online scheduling across multi-edge nodes.
workload_or_benchmark: Distributed edge LLM inference with spatiotemporal query correlations; models, node count, expert capacity, traces, and quality metrics are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Multiple resource-constrained edge nodes communicating for MoE inference; network, memory, accelerator, and fine-tuning costs are unspecified.
limits: The description omits model quality, communication volume, node heterogeneity, trace characteristics, and baseline configurations.
Latency claim may depend on expert-cache capacity and query correlation assumptions.
Official description only; system-level claim requires paper-level verification.
